features.description: AI pair programming in your terminal: launch aider with the files to edit and request changes at the > prompt.
aider --browser launches an experimental web UI to collaborate with LLMs and edit code in the local git repo.
Official docker images: paulgauthier/aider core and aider-full with extras such as the browser GUI and Playwright web scraping.
Default chat mode in which aider edits your code to satisfy requests.
Discuss the codebase and get answers without making any file changes.
A main architect model proposes how to solve the request and a separate editor model turns the proposal into file edits (--editor-model).
Answers questions about aider usage, configuration and troubleshooting.
Switch mode per message (/code, /architect, /ask) or stickily (/chat-mode, --chat-mode); the prompt shows the active mode.
About 50 slash commands including /add, /drop, /diff, /commit, /git, /run, /test, /lint, /tokens, /undo, /paste, /voice and /web.
Aider commits every edit with a descriptive commit message and offers to create a git repo if none exists.
/undo instantly undoes the last commit if it was made by aider.
Pre-existing uncommitted changes are committed first so user edits stay separate from AI edits.
Aider-authored commits get an (aider) author/committer name suffix, with optional aider: message prefixes and Co-authored-by trailers.
Commit messages (written by the weak model) follow Conventional Commits by default; customizable via --commit-prompt.
/diff, /commit and /git in-chat commands plus --no-auto-commits, --no-dirty-commits, --no-git and --git-commit-verify flags.
A concise tree-sitter-based map of the whole repo (key classes, functions, signatures) is sent with every request; tunable via /map and --map-tokens.
Repo maps and built-in linters cover most popular languages; edited files are linted automatically and aider offers to fix errors.
Connects to most LLMs: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, GROQ, xAI, Cohere, Azure, Vertex, Bedrock, OpenRouter, GitHub Copilot, LM Studio, Ollama and OpenAI-compatible APIs.
Separate models for editing, commit messages and summaries, switchable in chat via /model, /weak-model and /editor-model.
--alias fast:gpt-4o-mini style shorthand names for frequently used models, defined on the CLI or in config files.
/reasoning-effort and /think-tokens tune reasoning effort and thinking budgets; popular reasoning models work out of the box.
--cache-prompts organizes the system prompt, read-only files, repo map and chat for Anthropic and DeepSeek prompt caching.
/voice records and transcribes spoken coding instructions so you can fluidly mix voice and text chat.
Add images for vision-capable models via /add, /paste or CLI args; /web scrapes a URL to markdown and sends it in the chat.
--watch-files scans the repo for one-line AI, AI! or AI? comments written in any IDE or editor and acts on them.
Built-in or custom linters (--lint-cmd, per-language) run after edits; --no-auto-lint disables; /lint lints in-chat or dirty files.
--test-cmd with --auto-test runs tests after changes; /test adds failing output to the chat so aider can fix it.
--message and --message-file run a single instruction then exit; --yes auto-confirms, enabling scripted CLI and Python automation.
YAML config file loaded from the home directory, git repo root or cwd, with a --config override.
API keys and settings stored in .env files (home directory, repo root, cwd or --env-file).
A markdown file like CONVENTIONS.md loaded read-only via --read or /read-only sets style and library preferences.
/read-only adds reference files the model can see but never edit; kept stable so they can be prompt-cached.
/tokens reports token usage of the current chat context.
/editor (Ctrl-X Ctrl-E) composes the next prompt in your configured external editor.
{...} brace blocks, Meta-Enter, /multiline-mode and /paste for long messages; prompt-toolkit Emacs keybindings plus --vim Vi mode.
Control-C always safely interrupts aider; the partial response stays in the conversation for follow-up.
/save and /load write and replay files that reconstruct the current chat session file set.
/run executes a shell command (alias !) and can add output to the chat; /git runs raw git commands.
--notifications sends OS notifications (terminal-notifier, notify-send, PowerShell) when aider is waiting for input.
--copy-paste and /copy-context let you pair aider with LLM web chat UIs when APIs are unavailable or restricted.
Multiple LLM edit formats (whole, diff, diff-fenced, udiff and editor variants) selectable via --edit-format / --editor-edit-format.
Prefills the assistant response so models supporting prefill can continue past provider output token limits.
Edits almost any text file: shell and ssh configs, Dockerfiles, documentation and other config formats.
Anonymous, opt-in analytics collection with no personal information.
